We have applied first three templates: 20810 gave two products: product1 = "CC(C)(C)OC(=O)N1CCN(c2cc(N)cc3c2OC2(CCC2)CC3)CC1" and product2 = "O=S(=O)(Cl)c1ccccc1F". The route must use templates in order: ['20810','2895','1914397','1914398','1914399','74054'].

We need at least 6 reactions, using these templates in this order. So we need to apply each template sequentially to appropriate intermediate(s) to eventually get target molecule.

We have applied 20810 to target, got two fragments. The target is a sulfonyl urea? Actually target SMILES: O=S(NC1=CC(N2CCN(C(OC(C)(C)C)=O)CC2)=C3C(CCC4(CCC4)O3)=C1)(C5=C(F)C=CC=C5)=O. That's a sulfonamide linking aromatic ring with fluorophenyl sulfonyl group and a side chain with piperazine and t-butyl carbamate.

Our first step (retro) should break the sulfonyl group? Template 20810 likely corresponds to disconnection of sulfonyl chloride? The result gave a t-butyl carbamate piperazine fragment and a sulfonyl chloride aromatic fragment (Cl). So we have two fragments: fragment A (the piperazine side chain) and fragment B (the sulfonyl chloride aromatic with F). Good.

Now we need to apply template 2895 to fragment A (since we checked matching true). Applying 2895 gave a nitro-substituted aromatic fragment plus the same piperazine carbamate? Actually result: ("CC(C)(C)OC(=O)N1CCN(c2cc([N+](=O)[O-])cc3c2OC2(CCC2)CC3)CC1",). So it transformed the aromatic amine (N) to nitro? So we have new fragment: same piperazine side chain but aromatic now has nitro group instead of amine.

Now apply 1914397 to that molecule gave two fragments: "CC(C)(C)OC(=O)N1CCNCC1" and "O=[N+]([O-])c1cc(Br)c2c(c1)CCC1(CCC1)O2". So we split the aromatic nitro-bromo fused ring? Actually we got a fragment of the piperazine side chain without aromatic (just carbamate piperazine) and a aromatic fragment with nitro and bromo and bicyclic.

Now apply 1914398 to the aromatic fragment gave "BrBr" and "O=[N+]([O-])c1ccc2c(c1)CCC1(CCC1)O2". So it removed a bromine? It gave BrBr (bromine dimer) and the aromatic fragment now without bromine? Actually original had Br substituent; after applying template, we get BrBr (maybe leaving group) and the rest.

Now we need to apply 1914399 to something, then 74054 to finish to target.

We need to continue retrosynthesis: after 1914398 we have fragment "O=[N+]([O-])c1ccc2c(c1)CCC1(CCC1)O2". This is likely the core aromatic fused with nitro and a bicyclic ring (maybe a phenyl fused to cyclohexanol). The target aromatic part is "c1=CC(N2CCN(C(OC(C)(C)C)=O)CC2)=C3C(CCC4(CCC4)O3)=C1". That's a phenyl with a side chain (piperazine) attached at position, and a fused cyclohexanol ring. The nitro must be replaced by amine (N). So template 1914399 likely converts nitro to amine? Let's check matching.

We need to apply 1914399 to the nitro aromatic fragment to get an amine aromatic fragment. Let's test matching.
